title: Execute a stack instruction stream
description: You can follow the VM's instruction pointer and operand stack through a small arithmetic chunk.

steps.description: Chunk holds instructions. CallFrame stores the current instruction position and advances it when read returns an instruction.
The VM keeps an operand stack, frames, and globals. Its dispatch loop reads from the current frame and handles pushes and stack operations.

steps.question: After pushing 2, 3, and 4, what does ADD leave on the stack?
steps.answer: It pops 4 and 3, then pushes their sum, leaving [2, 7].

steps.description: Arithmetic and comparison cases pop right before left. Each operation pushes its result; division checks its divisor before calculating.
Variable loads check local and global dictionaries. Jump instructions change the instruction pointer, and conditional jumps also pop a test value.
CALL collects arguments and appends a frame. RETURN removes a frame and pushes its result; PRINT pops a value to display.
The first table prints supplied stack descriptions. The later chunk actually executes the five instructions and returns 14.
